questions.question: You are meeting a friend for lunch, but you are running late. What is the most appropriate way to apologise?
options: I'm afraid I won't be able to make it.
Sorry, I got held up at work.
I'm really sorry, but I can't come.
My apologies, I won't be there on time.
questions.answer: Sorry, I got held up at work.

questions.question: Your friend suggests going to a new restaurant. How should you respond if you think it's a good idea?
options: That sounds great!
I don't know yet.
What do you think?
Let's do it another time.

questions.question: A colleague proposes a new idea for the project. How should you disagree without being rude?
options: I'm not sure I agree with that.
That's not right at all.
I think you're mistaken.
I disagree completely.
questions.answer: I'm not sure I agree with that.

questions.question: You need to ask a neighbour to keep an eye on your house while you're away. What is the best polite way to request this?
options: Could you possibly keep an eye on my house?
I'm asking you to watch my house.
Please, you have to look after my house.
I'd be grateful if you could watch my house.
questions.answer: I'd be grateful if you could watch my house.

questions.question: You receive help from a stranger. How should you respond to show appreciation?
options: Thank you very much.
I appreciate that.
Thanks a lot for your help.
I'm grateful to you.
